title: Disable and remove
summary: Retirement deletes nothing and keeps history readable. It disables the project's active deployment flows, turns GitHub issue sync off and marks its GitHub repository binding unavailable; installation refreshes and lifecycle deliveries leave that binding off until an operator runs github-binding check or bind. Retire prints what stays attached, stored credentials (secret names, never values) first, each kind with the existing command that removes it or a plain statement that none does. Retired projects refuse item writes, claims, launches and deployment creation with project_retired; upkeep and fleet reports skip them. Unretire restores admission only: flows, sync and the binding stay off and it prints the command that re-enables each; because it lists every disabled flow, re-enable only the flows retire reported as switched off. Open items, active runs and held claims block retirement.
